text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.

Political Economy secretary Jose Roberto Mendonca de Barros predicted the Brazilian economy would be subjected to periods of "turbulence" in 1997 as the Real Plan continued to consolidate. "People who don't understand this will die of a heart attack. This is a long non-linear process which will generate a great deal of anxiety in financial markets," Mendonca de Barros said in an interview.

A federal court's decision to authorise a six year-old capital increase of Telebras stock has triggered a rush for the 1990 subscription recipts as the market believes the company will win an appeal and transform them into stocks.
The price of Telebras subscription receipts jumped 90 percent and the lot of 1,000 closed at 43.49 reais.
-- CIVIL SERVANTS GIVEN 1 MONTH TO JOIN VOLUNTARY RETIRMENT

Civil servants will be given one month to decide whether they want to sign up for a government voluntary retirement plan that will be launched in the second half of November. Finance Ministry officials estimate the retirement plan will carry a 900 million reais price tag.
-- POLICE PREVENT EXPLOSION IN RIO METRO

The Explosives branch of Rio's Police Department disassembled a 300 gram time bomb that had been left in a central Metro station. The bomb threat forced officials to close down five Metro stations for three hours in the middle of the evening rush hour.
-- FEDERAL DEFICIT HITS 2.3 BILLION REAIS IN SEPT
The Treasury's deficit hit 2.3 billion reais in September, the government's worst performance since April when government outlays exceeded income by 2.5 billion reais.
The accumulated deficit for the first three quarters is of 8.9 billion reais or 1.87 percent of GDP.
-- BRAZILIAN ARMY CLEARS VALE DO RIO DOCE GOLD MINE
A joint army and police raid opened access to a Vale do Rio Doce gold mine in the Northern Brazilian state of Para, in which 13 wildcat miners were arrested.
